title: The one inequality the LLL induction is really about
content: Open question OQ-01 asks for the genuine **measure-theoretic** Lovász Local Lemma. The sibling entry `lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01-chain-rule` reduced the whole problem to a single per-event obligation — bound each conditional failure probability $\mu[A_k \mid \bigcap_{j<k} A_j^c] < 1$ — but that scaffold is pure telescoping and never touches the dependency structure. This file supplies the piece that actually uses it: the arithmetic step of Spencer's LLL induction. There one bounds a conditional failure probability by splitting its survival history $H = C \cap B$, with $C$ the survivals of the current event's graph **neighbours** and $B$ the survivals of its **non-neighbours**, and estimating $\mu[A \mid C \cap B] \le \mu[A \mid B] / \mu[C \mid B]$. The numerator later collapses to $\mu(A)$ by independence of $A$ from the non-neighbours; the denominator is bounded below by the induction hypothesis. The inequality proved here is **completely general** — no independence, no graph, no LLL hypothesis — isolating exactly the measure-theoretic content of the step and leaving the independence collapse and the induction-hypothesis bound as the remaining open inputs.
mathContext: Arbitrary measurable $A, B, C$ over an `IsProbabilityMeasure` $\mu$ with $\mu(C \cap B) \neq 0$; goal $\mu[A \mid C \cap B] \le \mu[A \mid B] / \mu[C \mid B]$, no independence hypothesis.

title: The probability-space frame
content:
```lean
import Mathlib.Probability.ConditionalProbability
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped ENNReal
namespace LovaszLocalLemmaOQ01ConditioningQuotient
variable {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
variable {A B C : Set Ω}
```

The entire development runs over an arbitrary `IsProbabilityMeasure` $\mu$ and three arbitrary sets $A, B, C$. Two consequences of `IsProbabilityMeasure` drive the proof: it gives `IsFiniteMeasure`, so Mathlib's telescoping identity `cond_mul_eq_inter` ($\mu[t \mid s] \cdot \mu\,s = \mu(s \cap t)$) is available and every measure is $\neq \infty$, which is exactly what the $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^\infty$ cancellation `ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_left` needs. Only $B$ and $C$ are required to be measurable in the results (via explicit `MeasurableSet` hypotheses); $A$ is completely arbitrary, since it enters only through the monotone quantity $\mu(\cdot \cap A)$.
mathContext: All measures valued in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^\infty$; `IsProbabilityMeasure` supplies finiteness (for cancellation) and the telescoping identity `cond_mul_eq_inter`.

title: The division-free core: cancel μ B, telescope, and use monotonicity
content:
`cond_inter_mul_cond_le` proves the multiplicative heart of the step, $\mu[A \mid C \cap B] \cdot \mu[C \mid B] \le \mu[A \mid B]$, with **no division and no independence**. The side condition $\mu(C \cap B) \neq 0$ forces $\mu B \neq 0$ (since $C \cap B \subseteq B$, via `measure_mono_null`) and $\mu B \neq \infty$ (probability measure), so a common factor of $\mu B$ can be cancelled from both sides using `ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_left`. After multiplying through by $\mu B$, three applications of the telescoping identity `cond_mul_eq_inter` collapse every conditional:

$$\mu[A \mid C \cap B]\cdot\big(\mu[C\mid B]\cdot\mu B\big) = \mu[A\mid C\cap B]\cdot\mu(B\cap C) = \mu[A\mid C\cap B]\cdot\mu(C\cap B) = \mu(C\cap B\cap A),$$

and the right side becomes $\mu[A\mid B]\cdot\mu B = \mu(B\cap A)$. The goal is now the pure set-monotonicity $\mu(C \cap B \cap A) \le \mu(B \cap A)$, discharged by `measure_mono` on the inclusion $C \cap B \cap A \subseteq B \cap A$ (`fun x hx => ⟨hx.1.2, hx.2⟩`). Every step is elementary; the mathematical content of the LLL is *not* here but in the two inputs that later bound the numerator and denominator.
mathContext: $\mu[A \mid C \cap B] \cdot \mu[C \mid B] \le \mu[A \mid B]$ via cancellation of $\mu B$ and $\mu(C \cap B \cap A) \le \mu(B \cap A)$.
prerequisites: ℝ≥0∞ multiplicative cancellation with a finite nonzero factor

title: The quotient form quoted in the LLL literature
content:
`cond_inter_le_div` reformulates the core as the quotient bound $\mu[A \mid C \cap B] \le \mu[A \mid B] / \mu[C \mid B]$ — the shape that appears verbatim in Spencer's and Alon–Spencer's proofs. The conversion from the multiplicative core needs the denominator $\mu[C \mid B]$ to be (i) strictly positive and (ii) finite. Positivity is `cond_pos_of_inter_ne_zero hB` applied to $\mu(B \cap C) 
eq 0$ (the hypothesis after `Set.inter_comm`). Finiteness follows because conditioning on the positive-measure set $B$ yields a genuine probability measure — `cond_isProbabilityMeasure hBne` installs the `IsProbabilityMeasure (μ[|B])` instance, so `measure_ne_top` gives $\mu[C \mid B] 
eq \infty$. With both facts, `ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le` (whose disjunctive side conditions are met by $\mu[C\mid B] 
eq 0$ and $
eq \infty$) turns the goal back into the already-proved core. This is a cosmetic — but genuinely useful — repackaging: division in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^\infty$ is delicate, so the honest work was done multiplicatively and only exposed as a quotient here.
mathContext: $\mu[A \mid C \cap B] \le \mu[A \mid B] / \mu[C \mid B]$; denominator positive (`cond_pos_of_inter_ne_zero`) and finite (`cond_isProbabilityMeasure`).
prerequisites: conditioning on a positive-measure set is a probability measure

title: Packaging: numerator/denominator inputs to the failure bound < 1
content: The final two results deliver the step in the exact form the LLL induction produces and the chain-rule scaffold consumes. `cond_inter_le_of_num_den` takes a **numerator bound** $\mu[A \mid B] \le t$ — supplied in the LLL by independence of $A$ from the non-neighbour survivals $B$, collapsing $\mu[A\mid B]$ to $\mu(A)$ — and a **denominator lower bound** $q \le \mu[C \mid B]$ — supplied by the induction hypothesis, typically $q = \prod_{j\in S_1}(1-x_j)$ — and concludes $\mu[A \mid C \cap B] \le t/q$. The proof is the chain $\mu[A\mid C\cap B]\cdot q \le \mu[A\mid C\cap B]\cdot\mu[C\mid B] \le \mu[A\mid B] \le t$ (`gcongr` for the first step, the core for the second), read through `ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le`. The mild disjunction $q \neq \infty \lor t \neq \infty$ is free in the LLL setting where $t, q \le 1$. Finally, `cond_inter_lt_one_of_num_den` adds the hypothesis $t/q < 1$ and concludes $\mu[A \mid C \cap B] < 1$ by transitivity — **precisely** the per-event input that `avoidance_pos_of_failure_cond_lt_one'` in `lovasz-local-lemma-oq-01-chain-rule` turns into global avoidance positivity. This is the seam where a single induction step meets the global conclusion.
mathContext: From $\mu[A\mid B]\le t$ and $q\le\mu[C\mid B]$: $\mu[A\mid C\cap B]\le t/q$; with $t/q<1$, $\mu[A\mid C\cap B]<1$.
